title: Negation 4: Ни...ни... and Emphatic Ни
description: Russian uses the particle ни to coordinate two negated items ('neither bread nor milk') and to add emphasis to a noun in a negated sentence ('not a single word'). Both uses keep the not-yet-familiar but mandatory не on the verb.
descriptionRussian: Частица «ни» в русском соединяет два отрицаемых элемента («ни хлеба, ни молока») и усиливает существительное в отрицательном предложении («ни одного слова»). В обоих случаях обязательное «не» при глаголе сохраняется.
intro: By the end of this lesson you will be writing sentences that carry three separate negative words, all of them required, none of them canceling the others. That is the point where Russian negation stops being English with extra steps and becomes its own system. Read the examples slowly and count the negatives. Learners who economize here, dropping one because it feels redundant, produce the most recognizably foreign mistake in the language.
rules: Ни...ни... coordinates two negated items. The verb (or the нет construction) still takes its own не / нет. У меня нет ни хлеба, ни молока.
Each ни appears before the item it negates. The coordinated items can be nouns, verbs, adjectives, or short clauses.
Ни одного (masc / neut gen) and ни одной (fem gen) is the emphatic 'not a single' quantifier. The noun lands in the genitive after the quantifier. Не + verb is mandatory.
Ни is never a free-standing negation. It always pairs with another negation (не on the verb, or the нет construction).

The -нибудь family (что-нибудь, кто-нибудь, где-нибудь) appears in affirmative non-specific contexts (questions, conditionals, 'something / anything'). Never combine -нибудь forms with не on the verb.
In speech, не and ни sound similar but mean different things. Не negates a target; ни marks an item as part of a negated set. Both can co-exist in one clause.
examples: У меня нет ни ручки, ни карандаша. (I have neither a pen nor a pencil.) Two coordinated nouns in the genitive after нет.
Маша не любит ни кофе, ни чай. (Masha likes neither coffee nor tea.) Two coordinated accusatives after любит; the verb keeps its не.
Он не сказал ни одного слова. (He did not say a single word.) Ни одного + masculine gen слова; не on the verb.
Она не прочитала ни одной книги. (She did not read a single book.) Ни одной + feminine gen книги; не on the verb.
Лена не работает ни в субботу, ни в воскресенье. (Lena works neither on Saturday nor on Sunday.) Two coordinated в-phrases; the verb keeps its не.
Антон не знает ни Машу, ни Лену. (Anton knows neither Masha nor Lena.) Two coordinated accusatives; не on the verb.

rows.label: Possession
cells: У + person-gen + нет ни X-gen, ни Y-gen
У меня нет ни ручки, ни карандаша.

rows.label: Verb negation
cells: не + verb + ни X, ни Y
Маша не любит ни кофе, ни чай.

tables.title: Не versus ни at a glance

rows.label: не
cells: Negates the target word (verb, noun, adjective, adverb)

rows.label: ни
cells: Marks an item as part of the negated set (always with не on the verb)

items.hint: Recap from Lesson 3: the English object is 'anything / nothing.'
items.explanation: Warm-up from Lesson 3. Ничего marks a non-person thing as belonging to the negated set. The mandatory не sits on the verb помню.

items.promptEnglish: I have neither a pen nor a pencil.
items.hint: The English 'neither...nor.' Which Russian pair fits?
items.explanation: Russian uses the particle ни before each coordinated negated item. The нет construction also stays in place; both ручки and карандаша are in the genitive as required by нет.

items.promptEnglish: He did not say a single word.
items.hint: Ни одного triggers the genitive on the following noun.
items.explanation: The emphatic quantifier ни одного always takes a noun in the genitive. Слово is neuter ending in -о; its genitive is слова (-о → -а). The verb keeps its mandatory не: 'не сказал ни одного слова.'

items.promptEnglish: Masha likes neither coffee nor tea.
items.hint: Two coordinated negated objects after a regular verb. Which pair?
items.explanation: Ни...ни...Coordinates two negated items. Both coffee and tea are excluded; the verb любит keeps its не. The accusative case (любит + acc) applies to both nouns, but кофе and чай happen to look the same in nominative and accusative because they are masculine inanimate.

items.prompt: Лена не прочитала ни одной _____ за всё лето.
items.promptEnglish: Lena did not read a single book all summer.
items.hint: Ни одной triggers the genitive on a feminine noun.
items.explanation: The emphatic feminine quantifier ни одной takes the feminine genitive. Книга → книги (-а → -и after к, the standard spelling rule). The verb keeps its не: 'не прочитала ни одной книги.'

items.hint: This sentence is affirmative non-specific ('something'), not negative. Which family fits?
items.explanation: Affirmative non-specific 'something / anything' uses the -нибудь family (что-нибудь, кто-нибудь, где-нибудь). The verb is affirmative (хочу without не), so the ни-words do not fit.

blanks: В этом магазине нет ни молока, ни _____ . (In this store there is neither milk nor bread.)
fillInBlank.grammarFocus: Coordinated negation with ни...ни...After нет. Both items land in the genitive: молока and хлеба. Хлеб is masculine consonant; its genitive is хлеба.

minimalPairs.explanation: Affirmative non-specific 'something' uses что-нибудь. The verb хочу is affirmative; ничего would require не on the verb and flip the meaning to 'I do not want to read anything.'

minimalPairs.contextEnglish: I have neither a pen nor a pencil.
minimalPairs.explanation: Coordinated negation requires ни...ни... И...и...Means 'both...and...' and would describe affirmative possession, not absence.

errorCorrection.sentence: У меня нет и хлеба, и молока на завтрак.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I have neither bread nor milk for breakfast.
errorCorrection.explanation: И...и...Means 'both...and...' and is for affirmative coordination ('у меня есть и хлеб, и молоко', 'I have both bread and milk'). The нет construction is negative, so the coordinated items must take ни...ни...: 'нет ни хлеба, ни молока'. Mixing the two halves (ни...и...) is the most common A1 mistake; every coordinated negated item gets its own ни.

errorCorrection.sentence: Он сказал ни одного слова за весь вечер.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: He didn't say a single word all evening.
errorCorrection.explanation: The emphatic ни одного ('not a single') is part of a negated clause and requires не on the verb. Сказал alone leaves the construction unprotected; the ни-word demands a matching не. The correct form is 'Он не сказал ни одного слова'.

errorCorrection.sentence: Я ничего знаю об этой проблеме на работе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: I don't know anything about this problem at work.
errorCorrection.explanation: Recap from Lesson 3: every ни-word in a clause demands a matching не on the verb. Ничего знаю drops one half of the required double-negative pair and is ungrammatical. The correct form is 'Я ничего не знаю об этой проблеме'.

errorCorrection.sentence: Маша не работает ни в субботу и в воскресенье на этой неделе.
errorCorrection.translationEnglish: Masha doesn't work either Saturday or Sunday this week.
errorCorrection.error: ни в субботу и в воскресенье
errorCorrection.correction: ни в субботу, ни в воскресенье
options: ни в субботу, ни в воскресенье
и в субботу, и в воскресенье
не в субботу, не в воскресенье
errorCorrection.explanation: When two coordinated items are negated, BOTH halves must take ни. Mixing ни with и in the second slot ('ни...и...') is a frequent learner mistake but not grammatical. The correct pair is ни...ни...: 'не работает ни в субботу, ни в воскресенье'. The ни repeats on every coordinated item, no matter how many there are.

reviewVocab.definition: ни...ни... (the coordinating particle 'neither...nor'; appears before each negated item; the verb still takes its own не or the construction uses нет)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «У меня нет ни ручки, ни карандаша» «ни...ни...» соединяет два отрицаемых существительных.

reviewVocab.definition: ни одного / ни одной (the emphatic 'not a single (one)' quantifier; takes the noun in the genitive; requires не on the verb)
reviewVocab.example: В предложении «Он не сказал ни одного слова» «ни одного» подчёркивает, что не было сказано совсем ничего.

reviewVocab.definition: emphatic particle (a particle that intensifies the meaning of the next word; ни is the emphatic particle for negation)
reviewVocab.example: Частица «ни» в выражении «ни одной книги» — усилительная: она подчёркивает полное отсутствие.
